label: rejected

evidence.V1: Big domed spotted cap on a pale stem with a baby mushroom reads as a toadstool tree from front, three-quarter, silhouette and top (round spotted disc); clear at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Big cap, medium stem plus companion mini-mushroom, small cream spots and a lighter rim band: clear three-level hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised toadstool: oversized dome cap, slim slightly bowed stem, flared foot, child mushroom for scale contrast.
evidence.V4: Cap dome and rim are soft and rounded, but the stem foot flares end in hard polygonal rims and the spots are stuck-on domes with a hard contact edge; inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Base close-up shows low-segment faceting on the stem sides and polygonal foot flares; cap close-up shows faint grid shading on the dome. Minor but visible. (Gills close-up frames the cap side, so no gills are visible to judge.)
evidence.V6: Cap red in two values (top + lighter rim band) plus cream stem/spots; disciplined, strong value contrast; teal/ember colourways swap cleanly.
evidence.V7: 1600 tris vs tree target 2000 (ceiling 5000): under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, cream accent from the kit palette, smooth rounded forms; matches the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct.

evidence.V1: Classic domed cap on a stalk with a small companion mushroom reads instantly in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view is a spotted red disc, still a mushroom read.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: big cap and stem, medium companion mushroom and lighter rim band, small cream spots (only four, sparse).
evidence.V3: Cap shape is good, but the main stalk is a thin straight tube with a stiff flared foot; the stem lacks the chunky bulge or curve a confident stylised mushroom tree would have.
evidence.V4: Cap and rim are smooth and soft, while the stem foot flares and the small stem show hard low-segment facet rings, so edge treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Base close-up (studio) shows stray faceting on both stem flares and visible vertical facets on the stalks; cap rim band shows faint faceting along its edge.
evidence.V6: One cap hue in 2 values (red dome, lighter red rim) plus cream stem/spots; teal and ember colourways keep the same discipline.
evidence.V7: 1600 tris vs tree target 2000 - under target.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material and the right palette structure, but the low-segment faceted stems do not match the smooth weighted-normal organic shells the kit calls for; no gills visible under the cap despite a gills close-up.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Silhouette reads as a toadstool from front, 3/4 and side outline: broad dome cap on a tall stem plus a child mushroom; top view is just a spotted red disc but that is expected for a cap.
evidence.V2: Big cap / medium stem / small spots + child mushroom exist, but the small level is thin: only 4-5 spots, no visible gills or ring/skirt under the cap ('gills' close-up shows only the cap side), so mid detail is sparse.
evidence.V3: Cap-to-stem ratio is pleasantly chunky, but the main stem is a near-straight cylinder with a small foot flare and the child mushroom is a scaled copy; reads partly stylised, partly primitive.
evidence.V4: Organic fused shells are smooth, but cap rim outline and stem foot flare show visible polygon steps in the base close-up; spots have soft rounded edges; treatment is serviceable but uneven.
evidence.V5: No pinches, seams or z-fighting; minor faceting on the cap rim silhouette and foot flare in the base close-up, and a slight flat-shaded band at the cap underside edge.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one cap hue in two values (dark top, lighter rim band) plus cream stem/spots; colourways (teal, ember) swap cleanly.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material, smooth shading, cream #F3E3BE-like stem/spots and a single cap hue in 2 values; fits wave-2 nature kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, SmoothPlastic, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: Polygonal faceting on stem and foot flares
Faint grid shading on the cap dome
No visible gill detail; gills close-up camera does not look under the cap
Stray faceting rings on the stem foot flares (MushroomTree_01_close_base_studio.png)
Visible vertical facets on both stalks
Faint faceting along the cap rim band
Visible polygon stepping on cap rim outline and stem foot flare in base close-up
top_fixes: Add radial segments / weighted normals to the stems and round the foot flares so they shade smoothly
Add a gill underside (radial ridges in a darker cap value) and aim the gills close-up from below
Blend the spots into the cap (flatter, slightly sunk, 6-8 varied sizes) instead of 4 stuck-on domes
Raise stem segment count / smooth the flares with weighted normals so stalks shade as smooth organic shells
Thicken the main stalk and give it a slight curve or mid bulge for a chunkier stylised proportion
Add more spots in varied sizes and visible gill ridges under the cap for small-detail interest
Add an underside gill/ring detail (or skirt on the stem) so the medium/small tier is richer
Add a gentle bend/taper to the main stem and vary the child mushroom's proportions instead of a scaled copy
Raise segment count on the cap rim and foot flare (budget allows ~400 more tris) to remove silhouette stepping
Add 2-4 more spots of varied size to the cap
